airport.name: Miramar Marine Corps Air Station - Mitscher Field

summary: Miramar Marine Corps Air Station - Mitscher Field (NKX) is an active United States Marine Corps installation in northern San Diego, named after World War II naval aviator Admiral Marc A. Mitscher. It serves as a hub for Marine aviation operations and training, with no scheduled civilian commercial service. The field carries strong cultural ties to naval aviation lore, including its long association with carrier-landing training referenced in popular media.
faqs:
Q: Is NKX open to civilian or commercial passengers?
A: No, it is an active military installation and does not offer scheduled commercial airline service. Travelers should use San Diego International Airport (SAN) for commercial flights.

Q: Can private or general aviation aircraft land at Mitscher Field?
A: Operations are restricted to military and authorized aircraft. Civilian landings require prior coordination and military approval.

Q: What kind of aircraft and units operate from NKX?
A: It supports Marine aviation units flying both rotary- and fixed-wing aircraft, including squadrons historically tied to carrier qualification training.

Q: Where is the air station located within San Diego?
A: It sits in the Miramar community in the northern part of the city, adjacent to other military and aerospace facilities.
